issue_context.title: The default values of shard_row_id_bits and pre_split_regions should be configurable
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
The default values of shard_row_id_bits and pre_split_regions are 0, which make the customers have to set it one by one on their table schemas.

**Describe the feature you'd like:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Make the default values of shard_row_id_bits and pre_split_regions be configurable.

**Describe alternatives you've considered:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
No.

**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy:**
<!-- If you can, explain some scenarios how users might use this, situations it would be helpful in. Any API designs, mockups, or diagrams are also helpful. -->
When a new customer want to migrate his database to TiDB, we nearly always suggest them to set shard_row_id_bits and pre_split_regions on their tables, make the default values configurable will make the migration easier.

review_comments: I added the test for your comment https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/55717/files#r1743352402 , @Benjamin2037
If user manually set these two vars in create table or alter table statements, I think we should use user's define values. what do you think?
`handleTableOptions` is called on line 692, so it will overwrite the system variable setup here. Manually setup will always have a higher priority.
So here the system variable has higher priority than user manually specific?
No, manually setup has a higher priority.
Here，Before didn't we show warning message back to user or we directly use Maxvalue instead?
No warning here, we directly set to max.
